issues.title: [Ticket 20 / Slices 193–195] Complete real browser product journey
body: Reopen the claimed closure against the actual user-facing Web product rather than Battle Lab or fixture-only evidence.

Deliver Database, Army Builder, calculators, Settings/language, floating companion, authoritative room/map/models/threat, Preview/Apply/Replay, human-agent play, multi-game reflection, counterfactual branches and incremental Skill freshness as one coherent product journey.
Preserve Rules/Authority as the only legality source. Use one focused browser acceptance run per changed commit; only Critical/High findings block.

issues.title: [Ticket 14 / Slice 143] Complete Android physical-device acceptance
body: Produce the deferred Android package and real-device evidence after the Web/service journey is accepted.
The missing physical device is an external acceptance dependency; package preparation and non-device checks may proceed without claiming device closure.
Do not substitute an emulator or browser screenshot for the requested physical-device receipt.

issues.title: [Ticket 19 / Slices 196–201] Revalidate MuZero export from accepted real matches
body: Revalidate player-view observation/action/reward/discount/chance and recurrent-state lineage against the newly accepted H-A and A-A journals.
Prove hidden information does not leak and NDJSON/MuZero/RLDS round trips remain lossless.
Export eligibility stays separate from training; no learner is trained by this issue.

issues.title: [Ticket 21 / Slices 202–209] Revalidate production operations after product closure
body: Reconcile environment, RBAC, credential isolation, queues, releases, privacy, telemetry and incident evidence with the accepted product build.
Keep local demo, controlled experiment, production room and training-eligible run as distinct states.
External production approval remains explicit and cannot be inferred from local success.

issues.title: [Ticket 22 / Slices 210–214] Refresh final synthesis and acceptance bundle
body: Refresh requirement traceability, architecture and contract index, evidence/risk matrix, handoff runbook and final machine-readable acceptance after all reopened work closes.
Historical closure claims remain evidence, not substitutes for the final accepted product journey.
Run only the Ticket 22 aggregate after its dependencies are complete.

issues.title: [Ticket 23 / Slices 248–249] Repair live match sequencing, companion and reflection gaps
body: Preserve the recorded alternating-activation defect, combat-estimation/prediction-calibration gap, player-seat companion permission model and WikiSkill/EvoTest research as explicit follow-up work.
A fresh Standard-2000 match must start at revision 0 after the sequencing repair; the invalid historical match cannot become training truth.
Paid H-A/A-A and role-play runs require token/currency ledgers and user-visible reports.

issues.title: [Ticket 25 / Slices 262–263] Close spatial formation strategy and natural-match canary
body: Complete the agent-selectable formation/placement solver, position-reason output and natural-match formation canary.
Keep exact base-edge geometry, coherency, terrain, threat and Rules Preview binding; templates may seed search but may not replace free legal formation choice.
Validate strategy impact without promoting advisory geometry to authority.

issues.title: [Ticket 26 / Slices 264–266] Build and compare two StarCraft II companion role packs
body: Build two complete commander companion packs with character card, world book, era/relationship state, layered memory, tactical voice and Web floating-window integration.
Compare role fidelity, continuity, seat permissions, fact/inference separation, tactical quality, hallucination and immersion under identical model, Skill, tool and token budgets.
Kimi may implement scoped UI slices; Codex owns contracts, integration and final acceptance.
